$schema_note: task-063. The handful of combat-model dials the simulation harness (Scripts/sim/) needs that no gameplay-owned docs/data/*.json file has a row for. Everything else the harness uses (entity stat blocks, retinue tier HP/DPS, unit-type combat/formation dials, ArmorChipFloor, shared SwingInterval) is read live from entity-tiers.json / upgrades.json / unit-types.json — this file exists ONLY for the gap, not as a second source of truth for anything already owned elsewhere. Owned by task-063 (Scripts/sim/**, docs/sim/**, docs/data/scenarios/**), not by the gameplay director's docs/data/*.json set.

hero.Note: No docs/data/*.json file owns Hero combat stats (upgrades.json is the FRIENDLY RETINUE tier ladder, not the hero; entity-tiers.json is enemy tiers). These three numbers are read straight out of GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3's tuning history ('Hero at 120 DPS... soloed the tail of wave 3... Cut to 55 DPS. The hero is tanky (500 HP, max 8 attackers) but cannot replace the line.') and entity-tiers.md §7's own simulation notes, which used the identical figures for its Hero-solo-TTK table. SwingInterval assumed shared (GATE1 §3b: 'The hero runs the same cadence from SpikeHeroPawn... lands like everyone else's'). If upgrades.json or a future hero.json ever adds a real Hero row, this block should be deleted and the harness pointed there instead.

wave_attrition_model.MaxAttackersPerUnit_note: Swarm.MaxAttackersPerUnit shipped default (GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3b). Survives in the real sim only as a per-frame safety clamp on simultaneous strikers against one victim, not the primary damage-rate control anymore (geometric TargetsPerHit targeting is) — but it is exactly the 'how many bodies can pile onto one exposed victim' number this harness's frontage model needs, and the doc states it as a design default, not a per-instance dial, so one shared value is correct here.
wave_attrition_model.FormationSpacingUU_note: GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3a MEASURED (Swarm.SpacingReport): retinue ring formation at rest, median 86uu, min/max both 86uu (near-zero variance — it's an exact ring-slot geometry: '8r slots at radius 110r' gives arc spacing 2*pi*110/8=86uu). This is the ONE spacing number in this file that is measured, not estimated.
wave_attrition_model.EngagedSpacingUU_note: GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3a MEASURED mid-combat compressed spacing: min 25-39uu, median 43-51uu, max 343uu (outliers from units mid-knockback/mid-chase, excluded). 45uu is a round midpoint of the measured median band, used as the harness default. The frontage estimate this feeds (combat_model.exposed_frontage) is NOT itself measured — it is a Fermi circle-packing estimate that CONSUMES this measured spacing, same relationship entity-tiers.json's SurroundCapEstimate has to the same §3a data. Run docs/sim's scripts with EngagedSpacingUU set to 25 and 51 to see the model's sensitivity band before trusting a single number from it.
wave_attrition_model.MeleeContactFacingFraction_note: ADDED after review caught a structural bug: cleave (TargetsPerHit) capacity was originally bounded by reusing engaging_enemy_melee (the MaxAttackersPerUnit-capped INCOMING bound), which made the frontage term cancel algebraically and collapsed cleave's effect to a constant max_attackers_per_unit/targets_per_hit ratio regardless of any other dial (see docs/sim/VALIDATION.md). Fixed by deriving cleave capacity independently, off EngageRange, via combat_model.melee_reach_per_exposed_unit(). This fraction is that new function's one Fermi input: the share of the EngageRange circle around one exposed unit that is enemy-occupied territory rather than the unit's own formation's interior. 0.5 (an exposed perimeter unit's outward-facing half) is the harness default; 0.25/1.0 bracket it for sensitivity. NOT measured — same epistemic status as EngagedSpacingUU.
wave_attrition_model.model_status: This is the harness's own addition, not a value transplanted from a design doc. It generalizes entity-tiers.json's SurroundCapEstimate (built for a single point-target Elite/Titan/Boss) to a distributed retinue-vs-swarm formation. See docs/sim/MODEL.md for the full derivation, docs/sim/VALIDATION.md for the coupling bug this replaced, and docs/sim/LIMITATIONS.md for what it still can't capture (arrival/spawn-pacing timing).

variance_model.$note: task-076. The optional seeded variance layer (docs/sim/MODEL.md §4). MASTER GATE, above every flag in this block: nothing here has ANY effect unless a caller supplies a root seed (scenario_runner.run_trials(..., root_seed=...), or --seed on the CLI). With no seed, scenario_runner.run()/sweep.py/drift_check.py/validate.py's point estimates are bit-identical to the pre-task-076 harness no matter what these flags say — the variance layer cannot be switched on by editing this file alone. Each source below is either CITED (its magnitude traces to a shipped CVar or committed data file) or INVENTED (no citation exists); an INVENTED source additionally defaults to Enabled=false on its own, and any run with one enabled is flagged diagnostic in both the CLI banner and run_trials()'s `diagnostic_invented_variance` key. Same measured-vs-estimated register as the wave_attrition_model block above, and the same anti-fitting rule: docs/sim/LIMITATIONS.md §1/§6 — do NOT pick a Magnitude here because it widens a distribution toward GATE1's measured 109-111. A spread is not a confidence interval and cannot make validation check 3 pass.

arrival_jitter.Note: Swarm.BroodSpeedJitter, shipped default 0.06 (i.e. +/-6%), declared at ELVTR/Source/ELVTR/Mass/SwarmCommands.cpp:120 and rolled per spawned brood at SwarmCommands.cpp:306 as Rand.FRandRange(1 - SpeedJitter, 1 + SpeedJitter) — a UNIFORM draw on a speed SCALE. That is why this harness DIVIDES the nominal arrival time by the drawn factor rather than multiplying it: docs/data/encounter-budget.json's rank_arrival_formula is literally ArrivalSeconds = travel / (BroodSpeed * (1 +/- BroodSpeedJitter)). Both the magnitude and the distribution shape are read off shipped source, not chosen here. NAME CHECKED 2026-07-31 against shipped source: still Swarm.BroodSpeedJitter — task-093's Emberkeep.->Kindled. CVar rename did not touch the Swarm. prefix, so citing 'Kindled.BroodSpeedJitter' would be wrong.
arrival_jitter.ApproximationNote: Flagged plainly, because it is not part of the citation: the real sim rolls this ONCE PER ENTITY at spawn; this harness has no per-entity representation and rolls it once per WaveGroup, so a whole rank arrives early or late together. That overstates within-rank correlation, and therefore overstates the arrival spread relative to the real sim, where 60 independent draws per rank would largely average out. The magnitude is cited; this pooling is a harness approximation on top of it.
arrival_jitter.AppliesTo: wave_attrition only, and within it only to groups whose ArrivalSeconds > 0 (a group already in contact at t=0 has no travel time to jitter). Scenarios with no ArrivalSeconds rows produce zero spread from this source, correctly.

damage_roll.Status: INVENTED — the magnitude below is NOT measured and traces to no CVar, no committed data file, and no design doc. It is a made-up number.
damage_roll.Note: Per-tick multiplicative noise on each side's dealt damage, U(1-Magnitude, 1+Magnitude), drawn independently for the into-retinue and into-enemy totals. Stands in for the several real per-swing effects this pooled model has no primitive for (swing-phase desynchronisation across a population, per-hit target-selection churn, partial overkill) — none of which has a measured magnitude anywhere in this repo, which is exactly why 0.10 is invented rather than cited. Defaults OFF, individually, and any run that enables it is reported as diagnostic. Do not read a spread produced with this source on as anything but a sensitivity probe of the harness's own guesswork.
damage_roll.AppliesTo: wave_attrition (per tick, both directions) and point_target (one roll on the army's summed DPS, since that model has no time axis to roll along).
damage_roll.ObservedEffect: Run 2026-07-31 at Magnitude 0.10, 200 trials, root_seed 1234, gate1-calibration-wave1 (enabled via a --trials override, NOT by flipping Enabled in this file): enemy_survivors stdev 8.80 (vs 1.62 from arrival_jitter alone) and elapsed_seconds stdev 0.79, but retinue_survivors is 0.00 in all 200 trials and the outcome is retinue_wiped in all 200. So this source moves the loser's margin a lot and the verdict not at all. That is an observation about where this model is and isn't sensitive, and it is emphatically NOT a reason to raise the Magnitude until the distribution reaches 109-111 — see docs/sim/LIMITATIONS.md §6.
